newsitem.title: ITALY: France and Italy tighten Algerian guerrilla probes.
newsitem.headline: France and Italy tighten Algerian guerrilla probes.

text.p: A top French anti-terrorism investigator and Italian police agreed on Thursday to work more closely in investigating Algerian militants suspected of involvement in political violence.
"The French magistrate outlined his own investigative needs and I think we shall soon put our collaboration on a formal level," Turin's assistant police chief Maurizio Laudi told reporters.

He and other Italian police chiefs had a two-hour meeting in Turin with France's top anti-terrorism investigating magistrate, Jean-Louis Bruguiere, who led the probe into guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal", now in a French jail.
Bruguiere on Wednesday questioned in a jail in the southern port of Naples an arrested Algerian suspected of supplying arms to anti-government Moslem guerrillas in Algeria.
"Today's meeting was merely an initial contact," said Laudi, adding that they had agreed to closer ties.

"They are interested in the documents from our enquiries, while we need to question four or five Algerians detained in France, including one linked directly by Turin police in 'Operation Shakba'," Laudi said.
Nineteen people suspected of belonging to an Algerian guerrilla network were arrested in 'Operation Shakba', carried out by Italian police last month.
Bruguiere arrived in Naples on Wednesday to question Djamelk Lounici, who is suspected of ties to the armed wing of the Algerian Islamic Salvation front (FIS).
Lounici, 34, was arrested in Italy in May 1995 and is due to go on trial in Naples next April.
He is also awaiting extradition to France where he is being tried in absentia with 33 fundamentalists accused of backing Moslem guerrillas in Morocco.
The 33 were among nearly 200 Moslem fundamentalists detained after a wave of bomb attacks in France in 1995 in which eight people were killed and 160 injured.
